By Sandeep Giri

Learn By Inventing

Machine Learning & Computer Science — derived, not memorized.

Instead of starting with a formula or an explanation, every chapter here gives you a sequence of small problems. As you work through them, you begin to see the pattern yourself. By the end, you have not been taught an algorithm — you have invented one. That is the difference between knowledge you can recite and understanding you can use.

Read more about the philosophy →
How to use this Do not read this book. Work with it. Keep a coding environment open alongside each chapter. Each exercise is one small step — complete it before moving to the next. Resist the urge to look ahead. The struggle is the lesson.
0 Getting Started

Set up your coding environment and write your first Python program.

  1. Getting Started interactive ▶ Colab Set up Python in Colab or VS Code — variables, expressions, and your very first program.
  2. Line Fitting & Curve Fitting interactive ▶ Slides Predict from two points, handle noisy data, and fit curves — your first taste of regression.
  3. Finding Square Roots interactive ▶ Slides Guess, check, and halve the range — discover binary search by computing square roots.
I Math Foundations

Build number intuition before writing a single line of code.

  1. Learning to Count interactive Invent number systems from scratch — binary, octal, hex, and arithmetic in any base.
  2. Logarithms interactive ▶ Slides Count zeros, answer power questions, and build your own log function from repeated halving.
II Programming Fundamentals

Invent the core constructs of Python from first principles.

  1. Expressions & Functions notebook ▶ Colab Pull numbers apart digit by digit, build formulas as functions, and take your first derivative.
  2. If-Else notebook ▶ Colab Branch on a coin flip, compare distances, and check if points land inside rectangles.
  3. Loops and Arrays notebook ▶ Colab Compute min, max, mean, standard deviation, and detect outliers — one loop at a time.
  4. Recursion notebook ▶ Colab Multiply, exponentiate, find GCDs, and solve Tower of Hanoi — all by calling yourself.
  5. Dictionaries notebook ▶ Colab Count words, group anagrams, and invent hashing to discover why dictionary lookup is O(1).
  6. Classes & Objects notebook ▶ Colab Build a Customer, a sklearn-style line fitter, and a decision tree node — all as classes.
III Algorithms

Discover the classic algorithms that every engineer should understand deeply.

  1. Big O & Complexity interactive ▶ Colab Time your code, count steps, and discover why O(n log n) beats O(n²).
  2. Sorting notebook ▶ Colab Invent bubble, insertion, merge, and quicksort — then race them to see who wins.
  3. Binary Search & Approximations notebook ▶ Colab Halve your way to nth roots and logarithms, then search sorted arrays in O(log n).
  4. Trees & Heaps notebook ▶ Colab Evaluate expression trees, build a BST from scratch, and sort with a heap.
  5. Pattern Matching notebook ▶ Colab Match character by character, add ? and * wildcards, then graduate to regex on real logs.
  6. Backtracking notebook ▶ Colab Enumerate pairs, generate permutations, and solve Sudoku — by trying, failing, and undoing.
IV Machine Learning

Reinvent ML algorithms from scratch — no black boxes, no magic.

  1. The Encoder-Decoder Pipeline notebook ▶ Colab Parse CSV rows, map emails to integers, call a recommender, and decode its output.
  2. The Ancient Secrets of Prediction notebook ▶ Colab Invent dot products, cosine similarity, and matrix multiplication — the math behind prediction.
  3. Regression Losses interactive ▶ Colab Discover why errors cancel, then build MSE, MAE, and Huber loss from scratch.
  4. Differentiation slides ▶ Slides Compute slopes, discover the derivative as a limit, and handle functions of many inputs.
  5. Linear Regression & Gradient Descent notebook ▶ Slides ▶ Colab Descend the loss surface step by step to fit a line — then scale to many features.
  6. Decision Trees notebook ▶ Slides ▶ Colab Measure impurity, find the best split, and grow a full decision tree from scratch.
  7. Naive Bayes interactive Combine prior and conditional probabilities to classify, then fix the zero-frequency problem.
  8. Random Forests notebook ▶ Colab Bootstrap samples, randomize features, and average regression trees into a forest.
  9. Classification Metrics interactive ▶ Slides Build a confusion matrix, compute precision/recall/F1, and trace the ROC curve.
  10. K-Means Clustering interactive Assign points to nearest centers, recompute, repeat — invent K-Means clustering.
  11. Recommender Systems notebook ▶ Colab Normalize ratings, fill gaps with cosine similarity, and recommend from real class data.
  12. Neural Networks notebook ▶ Colab Wire sigmoid neurons, fight saturation, and watch a 2-neuron net fit an income-tax curve.
  13. Convolutions notebook ▶ Colab Load images as number grids, extract color channels, and slide filters to detect edges.
  14. Information Theory & Compression notebook ▶ Colab Design prefix-free codes, build Huffman trees, and discover Shannon entropy.
V Agentic AI

Build systems that learn, act, and reason autonomously.

  1. Reinforcement Learning interactive Play a game, write policies, and learn from rewards — invent reinforcement learning.
  2. RAG & Agentic AI interactive ▶ Colab Close the knowledge gap with search, invent RAG, add tool use, and build your first agent.

Apply everything — open-ended problems with no answer key.
